correctness.rationale: Invertibility ensures that each projective fixed point of the coordinate-square map followed by A-transpose yields one nonzero idempotent. The fixed-point polynomial is a nonzero homogeneous cubic, so K<=3. A uniform projective linear transformation sends any ordered triple of distinct points to any other with the same probability. Squaring identifies no inputs in characteristic two; otherwise it identifies just the (q-1)/2 nonzero opposite pairs. Their ordered pair and ordered triple collision counts are q-1 and 3(q-1)^2, respectively. The three factorial moments and total mass therefore yield the four M_j. Independent basis squares force automorphisms to be monomial. The diagonal kernel is trivial except for the zero-diagonal matrices, where it has size gcd(3,q-1); the swap condition and the nonzero idempotent equation there use the same cube-solvability condition. Any swap is an involution in the zero-diagonal case and inverts the diagonal kernel; this yields S3 when that kernel has size three. In the other swap stratum (ad nonzero, ca^3=bd^3), rescaling the basis yields diagonal entries 1 and common off-diagonal entry z with z^2!=1; for each allowed z there are exactly (q-1)^2 labeled matrices. There is one equal-coordinate idempotent. Off-diagonal solutions occur in a pair: in odd characteristic the difference squared is (1-3z)/((1-z)^2(1+z)), and the Möbius expression (1-3z)/(1+z) omits -1 and -3. In characteristic three -3 is zero, not a nonzero square. In characteristic two, off-diagonal solutions are parametrized by t^2+t=z/(1+z); the image of t^2+t is the trace-zero subspace, and 1 is the single excluded right-hand value, of trace m mod 2. These counts give R and leave the trivial-group row by subtraction. This argument covers q=2 and q=3 without any separability or group-scheme assumption, and the strata exhaust all matrices.
residual_risks: Uniform labeled invertible matrices only; not uniform isomorphism classes. Automorphism orders are rational point counts, not group-scheme lengths. Finite enumerations are corroboration, not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The first full perfect dimension gives a canonical all-matrix sample for questions about random algebra symmetries and rational idempotents. The additional coupling tells precisely how often order-two symmetry coexists with one versus three idempotents and separates field-size and characteristic effects through concrete trace and quadratic-character exclusions. This is a natural exact invariant not obtained by merely tabulating the already-known marginals or cyclic examples.
residual_risks: The statement is confined to perfect two-dimensional algebras and the labeled-matrix measure; downstream higher-dimensional behavior is not established.
